prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner-friendly site that explains crypto in plain English and shows real numbers (on‑chain data, charts, sources), or (B) an educator that also publishes its own trading performance and losses? Those are different — the latter is uncommon because of legal/marketing risks.

Here are good options depending on which you meant:

If you want plain-English fundamentals for beginners
- Andreas M. Antonopoulos — talks and books (Mastering Bitcoin / The Internet of Money). Very clear, technical intuition without jargon.
- Coin Bureau — extremely beginner-friendly guides and videos that walk through coins, wallets, safety, and how protocols work.
- CryptoCasey — step‑by‑step tutorials and explainers aimed at new users.
- Bankless — accessible guides focused on DeFi and how to actually use things (wallets, swaps, lending).

If you want plain-English material that also shows real numbers / transparent data
- Glassnode — on‑chain metrics and charts with clear methodology; good for seeing real network numbers.
- Messari — research and data dashboards that cite sources and show numeric analysis.
- Coin Metrics — reliable network and market data with transparent methodology.
- Dune Analytics — community dashboards show raw SQL queries and exact numbers; very transparent if you want to inspect the data yourself.

If you specifically want educators who publicly document their mistakes / trading journals
- This is rarer. Look for individual Substack authors and trading bloggers who run a public trading journal (search “crypto trading journal Substack” or “crypto trade log”). Some independent traders publish full trade lists and P&L, but there’s no single mainstream beginner site that consistently posts audited losses the way an investment fund would.
- For protocol/project postmortems and loss reporting (hacks, exploits), read The Defiant, CoinDesk investigative pieces, and Messari postmortems — they document real losses from attacks and bugs.

My short recommendation: for a beginner who wants plain English plus verifiable numbers, combine a plain‑English educator (Coin Bureau or Andreas Antonopoulos for fundamentals) with a data site like Glassnode or Dune so you can see the raw numbers yourself. If you want, tell me which focus you prefer (basic concepts, how to use wallets/exchanges, DeFi, or following live trades), and I’ll give a tailored short list — including a few individual trading journals if you really want people who publish wins and losses.
